newsitem.title: LATVIA: C.BANK OUTLINES MONETARY POLICY AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK OUTLINES MONETARY POLICY AGAIN.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank on Thursday once again outlined its blue print to move away from the currency board system and the reasons behind its wish to ditch the model.

"The currency board involves a number of short-comings that hamper the financial integration of Lithuania into the European Union," the director of the bank's policy division, Gintanas Nauseda, wrote in the Thursday edition of the English-language weekly The Baltic Times.
Under the currency board model, the central bank's role in monetary policy is passive.
In Lithuania, it guarantees that it will have one dollar in reserve for every four litas in circulation, freezing the rate at that level.
The central bank says that the system has done its job of maintaining monetary stability during a difficult stage of transition but says that its purpose will soon run its course.
Nauseda wrote that the currency board does not allow the central bank to deal with liquidity problems in the banking sector.
He also said that it made more sense to link the litas to a basket of European currencies as the country strives for EU membership.

The first stage of loosening the restrictions imposed by the currency board will involve the introduction of repo auctions, which are necessary to correct liquidity imbalances in the banking sector, Nauseda said.
In the second stage, the law on the stability of the litas will be amended to allow the central bank to back the litas in circulation will all of its assets.
In the third stage, to be launched no earlier than 1999, the central bank would begin the process of linking the litas to European currencies.
This would involve a transitional period linking the litas to both the dollar and the euro, which is to debut in 1999.
